newsitem.title: USA: Howard Gary firm not a target in probe - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Howard Gary firm not a target in probe - lawyer.

text.p: Municipal bond firm owner Howard Gary and his firm are not targets of the federal investigation into alleged corruption in Dade County, Fla, bond issues, but were instead the victims of extortion by "those in power," an attorney for Gary's firm said.
Attorney Peter Raben made the statements in a Sept 30 letter sent to Dade County Commissioners and to clients of the firm Howard Gary & Co Inc.
"Neither Mr. Gary nor the firm has been implicated in this investigtion and no charges, complaints, arrests nor indictments will be made against Mr. Gary or the firm," Raben's letter said.
His letter said that once the probe had ended and the facts were made public, it would be clear that "Mr. Gary was not the stalker, but the prey."

Raben said in the letter that Gary was contacted by U.S. Justice Department officals in connection with its investigation of corruption in public financing in Miami, and that Gary and his firm had cooperated fully.

"A Department of Justice probe into corruption in bond financing suggested that a public official was extorting a local bond company by demanding kickbacks from earned commissions in local publicly financed projects," the letter said. "When contacted by law enforcement officials, Howard Gary and Co cooperated fully in the probe directed at the financial demands placed upon the firm."

The letter stated, "The investigation revealed that Mr. Gary was compelled to kick back a significant portion of earned fees to those now under investigation in order to maintain a role in public financing projects in Dade County."
It added, "Contrary to recent uninformed pundits, Mr. Gary did not offer or attempt to bribe anyone; rather he was extorted by those in power and expected to pay for official protection."
U.S. prosecutors declined to comment, and Raben was unavailable for comment Friday. An official at Howard Gary & Co, citing company policy, also declined to comment.

Raben's letter was the first public statement about the federal probe on behalf of Howard Gary & Co, which was recently removed from a Dade County seaport bond issue because of the allegations in the press. The firm had been selected as senior manager for the $30 million deal.
The letter said the firm remained in good standing with regulators and continues to provide investment banking, underwriting and financial advisory services.
The letter did not identify anyone who allegedly demanded pay for "official protection" nor did it say how much money was involved.

Miami Herald has reported that Gary was present in a San Francisco hotel room when Dade County Commissioner James Burke discussed a $300,000 kickback with former California bond firm owner Calvin Grigsby.

The newspaper said on Sept 26 that the conversation was recorded on videotape and that "Gary was working with the FBI after being caught in Operation Greenpalm, the federal probe that uncovered a cash-for-contracts scheme at Miami City Hall."
In interviews with Reuters and other media, Burke has said the recorded conversation had been orchestrated by Gary.

Raben said in his letter that "misinformed commentary and self-serving statements of an inflammatory nature" had recently appeared in print and other media, and that it would be improper "to allow misstatements and other errors to go uncorrected." He did not cite any particular media report.
Neither Grigsby, Burke nor Dade County employees have been charged with any crime.
Burke and Grigsby have denied wrongoing. Burke's former chief of staff Billy Hardemon, who has acknowledged he is also a target of the probe, has also denied wrongdoing.
